How the project is coming together

Drilling and casing are done. Tank erection follows once the building is up.

This one is running alongside the construction of the rental apartment it will supply — the borehole came first, the water storage comes once the building can carry it.

  1. 01
    Hydrogeological survey
    Site investigation behind King David's Hospital in Ngong town to identify a viable drilling point and estimate the depth to a productive aquifer.
  2. 02
    WRA permit application
    Survey findings submitted to the Water Resources Authority to secure authorization to drill and abstract groundwater at the site.
  3. 03
    Drilling & casing
    The rig sunk the borehole to 250 metres, with steel casing installed the full depth to secure the well ahead of the building rising around it.
  4. 04
    Pump installation Upcoming
    A submersible electric pump will be set at working depth once the apartment's electrical and plumbing risers are ready to receive it.
  5. 05
    Tank erection Awaiting building
    Storage tanks go up on completion of the apartment block above, giving the supply the elevation it needs for gravity-fed distribution to the units below.

Where things stand

Cased and capped, waiting on the building above it.

The borehole is drilled, cased to 250 metres, and capped at ground level — secure and ready for the next stage.

Pump installation and tank erection are on hold until the apartment above it is far enough along to take the storage and plumbing. We'll update this page with photos of the finished installation once that work is done.
